 Judgment
The petitioner has filed claim application U/Sec 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the petitioner case as follows:-
On 27.02.2023 at about 11.15 p.m, after completion of his work the petitioner was riding two-wheeler bearing No.KA-11-EQ-8666 from Mathikere to Vidyaranyapura,
when he reached near BEL Flyover, by that time, one Tempo Traveller bearing (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.4898/2023 No.KA-54-5071 came from Kuvempu Circle, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle and caused the accident.
Due to this, the petitioner fell down and grievous injuries and vehicle also badly damaged.
Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Ramaiah hospital, Bengaluru, for treatment.
After discharge he took treatment at Prasad Global hospital, wherein he took treatment as per Discharge summary.
The petitioner repaired his bike at Dhruvdesh Motors Pvt. Ltd., Gokul Extension.
The petitioner has spent Rs.50,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance and repairs of his bike.
At the time of accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as a Driver and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, he is not able to attend his work.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of aforesaid offending Tempo Traveller by its driver and in this regard the Jalahalli Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of the Tempo Traveller.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending Tempo Traveller are jointly and severally (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.4898/2023 liable to pay compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- with cost and interest.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence, was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and has filed objections.

04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending tempo traveller, age, income,
occupation of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner.

Further admits issuance of policy in favour of the respondent No.1 in respect of tempo traveller and the liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the tempo travellier was not at all caused or involved in any accident and the alleged accident took place due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself and that driver of tempo traveller was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the said vehicle was not having valid permit and fitness certificate and hence (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.4898/2023 there is committed breach of terms and conditions of the Narendra vs Vijaya Kumar B N on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126679392/
2 policy by the respondent No.1.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and the compensation claimed is exorbitant and hence prays to dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs in both petitions.
05. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor:

-
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner is proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 27.02.2023 at about 11.15 p.m, near BEL on Flyover MES Ring Road, Mathikere, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of Tempo Traveller bearing registration No.KA-54-5071 by its driver as alleged in the petition ?
02.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
03 . What Order or Award?
06. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17 and closed his side evidence.
By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 submits no evidence.
Hence, the respondent No.2 evidence is taken as nil and closed its side evidence.

08. Heard arguments.
09.

My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1

In affirmative  Issue No.2 In partly affirmative  Issue No.3 As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- Petitioner filed affidavit as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments.

Though he has elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners regarding rash and negligent driving of tempo travellier by its driver the accused took place and petitioner sustained injuries.

On perusal of exhibited documents,
Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Jalahalli Traffic Police against driver of the Tempo traveller.

Ex.P.2 is the complaint which shows that, due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tempo Narendra vs Vijaya Kumar B N on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126679392/
3 traveller bearing No. KA-54-5071 the accident took place and petitioner (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.4898/2023 sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.3 is the Charge sheet filed against driver of the offending Tempo traveller due to his rash and negligent driving for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.4 and 5 are the Spot Mahazar and Sketch showing the place of accident on Mathikere - Vidhyaranyapura Road near 100 Feet BEL Flyover, which is not disputed.

Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate shows petitioner sustained right wrist swelling and tenderness present, right knee abrasion present tenderness present, right ankle tenderness present and left chest tenderness present and said injuries are simple in nature.
Ex.P.7 is IMV report which shows involvement of both vehicles in the accident and damages caused to its front side.
Ex.P.8 is Notice issued U/Sec 133 of IMV Act to the owner of the offending vehicle.

Ex.P.9 is Reply given by the owner stating that as on the date of accident one Pramod Rao was driving the offending Tempo traveller and he had valid driving licence and the said vehicle had valid insurance as on the date of accident.
Ex.P.10 is Order sheet in CC No.5501/2023 wherein the accused has pleaded guilty and paid fine of Rs.1,500/- before MMTC-III, Bengaluru.
Ex.P.11 is OPD Discharge card.
Ex.P.14 to 16 are the Aadhaar card, Driving (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.4898/2023 licence and RC of petitioner

and these documents clearly goes to show that, due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Tempo travellier the accident took place and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
To disprove the petitioner case, the respondent No.2 has not lead evidence.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of simple injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road traffic accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 39 years and was working as a Driver and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.50,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance and repairs of his bike.
Due to accidental injuries, he cannot do his normal work and sustained loss of income and has became permanent disabled.
12. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.4898/2023 he has produced Ex.P.14 and 15 are the Aadhaar card and Driving licence of petitioner.
Eventhough the said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other evidence, the same can be relied upon,
According to which, the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 04.06.1983.
The alleged accident occurred on 27.02.2023.
Therefore, it appears that at the time of accident the age of petitioner is 39 years.
Accordingly, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 39 years as on the date of accident.
13. As per Ex.P.6 Wound certificate the petitioner has sustained simple injuries.
The petitioner has not produced Discharge summary to show about inpatient treatment and has not produced medical expenses to show about expenses incurred.

Further, in this case the petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him and has not produced any disability certificate to show that he has sustained any physical or functional disability which is come in the way of his day to day life.
As per Ex.P.12 the petitioner has incurred Medical expenses of Rs.21,602/-.

Absolustely, there is no evidence on Narendra vs Vijaya Kumar B N on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126679392/
4 record to show that petitioner sustained any physical or functional (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.4898/2023 disability and no evidence on record to show his age, avocation and income.

sentences.text: There is no evidence on record to show that petitioner sustained loss of future income and loss of income during laid up period and also there is no evidence on record to show that petitioner requires further treatment.

Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.60,000/-.
14.
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.60,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
15. Regarding liability:- Despite service of notice, respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte.

On service of notice, respondent No.2 has appeared and filed written statement and contest the matter, but it has not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove its contention.
On the date of accident policy was in force.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.

(SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.4898/2023 Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.60,000/- (Rupees Sixty thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining his bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
